sentences.text: Under International rules, any vessel other than a vessel not under command or a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver shall, if circumstances admit, avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft that is showing the signals of Rule twenty-eight.
The vessel constrained by her draft shall navigate with particular caution, having full regard to her special condition.
Remember from Rule eight that not impeding means acting early to leave sea room.
It’s different from give-way and stand-on.
And remember that constrained by draft doesn’t exist under Inland rules.
